metadata.title: Universal Hybrid Experience Point System
metadata.purpose: A D&D 5.5e-compatible hybrid XP system combining shared and individual combat XP, milestone XP, equal-value alignment continuity and alignment evolution XP, class expression, and deity covenant development.

design_promises: Being true to an established alignment and changing alignment through a coherent choice are equally worthy of XP.
Alignment movement records demonstrated behavior and is never itself a reward, punishment, or prerequisite for leveling.
Combat XP is shared so support, control, healing, rescue, and nonlethal solutions remain valuable.
Individual combat XP recognizes exceptional contribution without rewarding kill stealing or damage competition.
Milestone XP rewards discoveries, relationships, objectives, and world changes, including noncombat solutions.
Class and deity material provides personalized prompts without taking control of a character away from the player.
No character loses XP, levels, or earned features for alignment change, covenant strain, failure, retreat, or moral complexity.

compatibility.official_thresholds: Uses the D&D character advancement XP thresholds for levels 1-20.
compatibility.total_character_level_rule: XP thresholds use total character level, not an individual class level.
compatibility.level_20_option: After 355,000 XP, every additional 30,000 XP can grant a bonus feat when the MOL uses the official post-level-20 advancement option; Epic Boon feats are especially appropriate.

calculation.level_gap: XP threshold for next total character level minus XP threshold for current total character level.
calculation.percentage_award: Round level_gap × tier_rate to the nearest 5 XP, minimum 5 XP.
calculation.level_20_gap: Use a 30,000 XP epic increment for percentage awards at level 20.
calculation.carryover: XP beyond a threshold carries forward. Leveling never erases excess XP.

party_combat_xp.default_rule: Add the XP values of all enemies and threats neutralized in the encounter, then divide the pool equally among all eligible participating PCs.
party_combat_xp.neutralization_equivalence: Defeat, surrender, capture, banishment, escape, negotiation, containment, or another lasting neutralization awards the same threat XP when it resolves the encounter objective.
party_combat_xp.eligible_participant: A PC who was present and materially exposed to the encounter, including a character who spent the encounter healing, controlling, scouting, negotiating, protecting civilians, or incapacitated after participating.
party_combat_xp.rounding: Round each share down to the nearest 5 XP; assign any remainder to a party milestone pool or discard it consistently.
party_combat_xp.summoned_creatures: Use the creature stat block and current D&D rule for summoned creature XP; the default table retains listed XP unless a specific rule says otherwise.
party_combat_xp.virtual_threats: For a combat-like hazard, chase, siege, ritual, or social confrontation without monster XP, award the low, moderate, or high encounter budget per character according to actual danger and resource pressure.

individual_combat_xp.purpose: Recognize exceptional, encounter-relevant contribution without tracking kills or raw damage.

examples: Meaningful setup, scouting, control, rescue, objective work, counterplay, or support that the party used.
A costly action prevents defeat, saves multiple lives, secures the objective, or enables the whole party.
A singular but team-compatible contribution radically changes a high-stakes encounter.

individual_combat_xp.formula: Round personal_party_share × tier_rate to nearest 5 XP.
caps: One individual combat award per encounter.
Maximum award is 25% of the PC’s party combat share or 3% of the current level gap, whichever is lower.
At least one other participant or the MOL must be able to state how the contribution changed the encounter.
not_awarded_for: Creating danger solely to solve it
Acting against party goals without prior player consent

story_beat: Reveal a useful clue, gain safe passage, repair a relationship, map a route, or secure a needed tool.
minor_milestone: Resolve a meaningful local objective or permanently change one NPC, site, faction, or settlement situation.
standard_milestone: Complete a quest lane, secure an alliance, prevent a serious threat, or make a consequential discovery.
major_milestone: Change a province-scale conflict, defeat a major antagonist, recover transformative knowledge, or alter a faction’s direction.
chapter_milestone: Conclude a campaign chapter and materially transform the party’s place in the world.
campaign_defining_milestone: Resolve or radically redirect a campaign’s central conflict.

milestone_xp.individual_milestones: Use the same rates for personal arcs only when the achievement is genuinely individual; otherwise award the party tier.
milestone_xp.overlap_rule: An event may award both combat XP and milestone XP when the combat resolves a threat and the objective also changes the story or world. Do not split a single milestone into several synonyms.

alignment_identity_xp.name: Identity XP

continuity_alignment_safe.definition: A meaningful choice authentically expresses the character’s current alignment profile, secondary axes, convictions, ties, class practices, or covenant without forcing score movement.
examples: A selfish character protects a valued ally at great cost for a coherent selfish, loyal, reputational, or legacy-based reason.
A ruthless character accepts surrender because the bargain is strategically necessary and consistent with established restraint or honor.

evolution_alignment_change.definition: A meaningful choice coherently departs from the established pattern and justifies actual alignment movement, a changed conviction, or a revised relationship to class or deity.
examples: A selfish character saves an unknown baby at real risk because compassion breaks through, creating Altruism movement.
A lawful character breaks a legitimate command after recognizing that obedience would violate a defining conviction.

tier_guidance.meaningful: A real choice with consequence, but limited cost, risk, or permanence.
tier_guidance.significant: A choice under pressure with clear cost, risk, sacrifice, or relationship consequence.
tier_guidance.major: A choice that changes a major relationship, duty, faction position, conviction, or axis pattern.
tier_guidance.defining: A campaign-shaping choice that confirms or transforms identity across multiple future decisions.

alignment_identity_xp.movement_separation: First award XP for the meaningful choice. Then adjudicate alignment movement separately using intent, freedom, knowledge, cost, foreseeable and actual consequences, principles, repair, and repetition.
alignment_identity_xp.single_choice_rule: One choice receives either Continuity or Evolution XP, never both. A complex choice may touch several axes but still receives one Identity XP tier.
alignment_safe_guarantees: No XP loss for changing alignment.
No XP loss for staying within alignment.
No automatic class-feature loss from alignment movement.
No forced movement for a single ambiguous act.
No requirement to choose the morally approved option.
No MOL veto merely because a choice is surprising; surprising choices require coherent motive or emerging change.
anti_farming: No XP for harmless repetition, filler dialogue, or declaring an emotion without consequence.
No XP for performing inconsistency solely to collect Evolution XP.
No XP for repeating the same choice without new stakes, cost, audience, or consequence.
Coerced conduct does not normally move alignment; the response to coercion may qualify.

class_expression_xp.default_stacking_rule: Class Expression XP may stack with combat or milestone XP. It normally does not stack with Identity XP for the identical personal decision; record both tags and award the higher personal tier unless the class achievement and identity choice were independently consequential.
class_expression_xp.multiclass_rule: Use total character level for values. Each class has its own prompts, but the combined Class Expression XP cap is 10% of the level gap per session unless a defining multiclass breakthrough occurs.

resolution_order: Identify the consequential choice and who controlled it.
Choose Continuity, Evolution, or no Identity XP.
Select tier based on cost, risk, permanence, and campaign effect.
Award XP using total character level.
Update profile name only if the four profile axes cross their conversion bands.
Update secondary descriptors when their bands change.
Record class, covenant, conviction, tie, reputation, Resonance, and Claim consequences separately.

session_targets.measured: About 15% of the current level gap per typical session.
session_targets.standard: About 25% of the current level gap per typical session.
session_targets.fast: About 35% of the current level gap per typical session.

pacing_and_caps.personal_development_soft_cap: Identity + Class Expression + Covenant XP should normally remain at or below 15% of the level gap per PC per session; a defining climax may reach 25%.
pacing_and_caps.total_soft_cap: Combat + milestone + personal awards should normally remain near the chosen pacing target. This is a planning guide, not a reason to erase already earned XP.
pacing_and_caps.spotlight_equity: Compare cumulative individual awards every 3 sessions. When one PC is more than 10% of a level gap ahead solely from individual awards, prioritize opportunities for other characters or temporarily convert individual distinctions into equal party awards.

attendance_options.strict: Absent PCs receive no session XP.
attendance_options.catch_up: Absent PCs receive party milestone XP but not combat or personal XP.
attendance_options.party_parity: All continuing PCs stay at the same total XP; individual awards become party XP. Recommended when attendance varies often.

before_session: Record each PC’s total level, current XP, level gap, alignment profile, secondary axes, convictions, classes, deity, Resonance, and Claim.
Choose a pacing target and likely milestone tiers.
Prepare at least one meaningful alignment-safe opportunity and one possible evolution pressure without predetermining the answer.
during_session: Track neutralized threats and objective completion.
Mark potential individual combat contributions without announcing a competition.
Ask motive only when it matters for alignment interpretation.
Do not decide alignment change before hearing the player’s intended reasoning.
end_of_session: Award at most one individual combat tier per encounter.
Review personal choices and award Continuity or Evolution XP at equal values.
Apply class and covenant awards using stacking rules.
Adjudicate alignment movement, Resonance, Claim, reputation, convictions, and ties separately.
Add all XP, carry excess, and resolve total-level advancement and class allocation.
dm_session_procedure.player_voice: The player states motive and intended identity meaning; the MOL adjudicates evidence, stakes, consequences, XP tier, and movement. Neither side unilaterally rewrites the character.

worked_examples.name: The Selfish Character Saves a Baby
worked_examples.situation: A character established as Selfish enters a burning home to save an unknown baby, risking death and losing valuable loot.
worked_examples.continuity_result: If the motive is coherent self-interest, loyalty to a personal code, reputation, leverage, or legacy, award Continuity XP. Altruism may move little or not at all depending on the full evidence.
worked_examples.evolution_result: If compassion for a stranger genuinely overrides self-interest, award Evolution XP and consider significant Altruism movement.
worked_examples.equality: Use the same Identity XP tier in either interpretation. The reward follows meaningful characterization, not moral approval.

worked_examples.name: The Merciful Character Executes a Possessed Ally
worked_examples.situation: A normally Merciful character has credible evidence that no cure remains and continued possession will kill a settlement.
worked_examples.result: The choice may earn Continuity XP if it is proportionate protection consistent with mercy’s distinction between threat and person, or Evolution XP if the character embraces a more ruthless direction. The same tier applies.

worked_examples.name: Victory Without Killing
worked_examples.situation: The party traps, bargains with, or banishes a dangerous enemy without reducing it to 0 HP.
worked_examples.result: Award full party combat XP when the threat is durably neutralized, plus milestone XP if the resolution changes the story or world.

worked_examples.name: Support Character Defines the Encounter
worked_examples.situation: A healer, controller, scout, or defender enables the party to survive and secure the objective while dealing little damage.
worked_examples.result: The character receives the same party share and may receive Individual Combat XP when the contribution meets a tier. Raw damage and final blows are irrelevant.

worked_examples.name: Deity Fidelity or Severance
worked_examples.situation: A covenant-bound PC either fulfills an edict at severe cost or rejects a divine demand to preserve autonomy.
worked_examples.result: Both can receive equal Covenant XP at the same tier. Resonance and Claim may move in opposite directions, but neither result removes XP.
